title: fix(react,components): make toRenderableSchema behaviour-preserving for the falsy primitives (objectui#8908)
body:
Fixes #8908

`toRenderableSchema`'s docblock promised "the value a caller forwards renders identically whether or not it passes through here". That is now true. It was false for exactly two of the six `SchemaNode` members, and the fix is in the bridge — the behaviour, not the docblock, per triage.

## What changed

`packages/react/src/schema-input.ts` — the mapping has two legs and mirrors `SchemaRenderer`'s own narrowing order instead of half of it:

```ts
return typeof node === 'number' || typeof node === 'boolean'
  ? (node ? String(node) : undefined)
  : node;
```

A truthy `number` / `boolean` still becomes its text form, which is what the renderer's defensive branch produces. A falsy one — `0`, `-0`, `NaN`, `false` — becomes nothing, which is what the renderer's `!evaluatedSchema` leg produces. `!node` is exactly that set for the two members this function converts, so the ternary IS the renderer's order.

## ⚠️ A fork the dispatch asked to be flagged: route 2 as literally worded is not available

The brief assumed route 2 — "guard the bridge so `0` / `false` pass through **unchanged**" — and asked me to stop and report if any call site would break under the resulting type widening. **It would, at every one of them**, so the delivered repair reaches the same behaviour without widening anything. Measured, not assumed:

- The return type is pinned **exactly equal** to `SchemaRendererProps['schema']` by `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.propsResolution.test.ts` (assertion 7, `Equal< ReturnType< typeof toRenderableSchema >, SchemaRendererProps['schema'] >`). Exact equality, so any widening fails it.
- The same file pins `number extends CallSiteProps['schema']` and the `boolean` twin as **false** (objectui#4548 ruling Q2). So widening the prop instead is blocked by the same suite from the other side.
- **32 call sites, and every single one is a direct `schema={toRenderableSchema(…)}` forward** into `SchemaRenderer` — 19 in shipped source (`apps/site` 5, `packages/components` 5, `plugin-detail` 6, `plugin-report` 2, `plugin-view` 1) and 13 in tests/examples. Not one calls a method on the result, spreads it, or narrows it. A widened return would therefore be a TS2322 at all 19 shipped ones — the exact failure the docblock records from PR #4608, which kept `Build Docs` red on `main` for ~5 hours.

⇒ Returning nothing for the falsy pair keeps the guarantee **and** the type. The published type face is byte-identical; only runtime behaviour moves. If you want the literal pass-through instead, that is a published-surface type break and it is yours to rule, not mine — say so and I will re-cut it.

## Acceptance — the card's own two tables, re-measured

Both are executable pins now, and both were measured on the pre-fix bridge during the ablation (the "before" columns are that run's actual output, not a restatement of the card).

Six-row raw-vs-bridged, `packages/react/src/__tests__/schema-input.bridgeFidelity.test.tsx`:

| value | raw | bridged (before) | bridged (after) | same |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | `""` | `"0"` | `""` | now true |
| `false` | `""` | `"false"` | `""` | now true |
| `42` | `"42"` | `"42"` | `"42"` | control, true both legs |
| `true` | `"true"` | `"true"` | `"true"` | control, true both legs |
| `""` | `""` | `""` | `""` | control, true both legs |
| `"txt"` | `"txt"` | `"txt"` | `"txt"` | control, true both legs |

Three-row `empty` renderer, `packages/components/src/__tests__/empty-action-falsy-primitive-8908.test.tsx`:

| `empty.action` | text (before) | text (after) |
|---|---|---|
| `0` | `"T0"` | `"T"` |
| `false` | `"Tfalse"` | `"T"` |
| `""` | `"T"` | `"T"` |

The four `same=true` rows are **live controls**: they are asserted on both legs of the ablation and stay green on both, so "renders nothing for everything" cannot pass as a fix. Every row asserts **both** facts the brief required — that the two paths agree, and the concrete text each one produced — because an agreement-only assertion passes on a harness where the two could never have disagreed.

## All six `SchemaNode` members are pinned, not just the broken two

Enumerated from the declaration (`packages/types/src/base.ts`), not from the card: `BaseSchema | string | number | boolean | null | undefined`. Each has an arm rendered raw-vs-bridged, including the whole falsy-number boundary (`0`, `-0`, `NaN`) and both truthy directions (`42`, `Infinity`).

The "cannot regress silently" half is mechanical, not a table someone has to remember to extend: `MEMBER_CASES` is a `Record< MemberName, Case[] >`, so every name needs an arm, and `_MembersAreExactlyCovered` pins `MemberName` to the declared union itself. Add a seventh member to `SchemaNode` and the file stops compiling until someone decides what it renders as.

## objectui#8331's truthiness leg: KEPT, and here is the explicit justification

Not removed, and not left to vanish as tidying. `data-table`'s `emptyAction` leg (`schema.emptyAction ? … : null`) **is now redundant** — with the bridge repaired, `0` / `false` reach the same answer whichever side decides it. It stays because:

1. It is what makes that slot's answer independent of the bridge, and that independence is precisely why `emptyAction` was never affected by this defect while `empty.action` was.
2. Its pins assert the OUTCOME, so they would stay green through a removal right up until the bridge regressed again. Removing the leg would spend a working guard to buy nothing.

Its rationale comment said the bridge is *not* behaviour-preserving for `0` / `false`. That was true when written and my change makes it false, so it is corrected in place rather than left to mislead — same for the docblock and one inline comment in `data-table-empty-action-primitive-node.test.tsx`, and for the bridge paragraph in `empty.tsx`. **No assertion in either existing suite was weakened, retargeted or deleted**; only prose moved. `SchemaRenderer.primitiveSchema.test.tsx` (objectui#4548's pin, the invariant this card restores) is **untouched** and green.

## Ablation — prediction written before the run, then compared

Predicted red set was recorded before running: **8 tests across 2 files**, named individually. Result: **8 failed | 69 passed (77)**, 2 files — every predicted name matched, no extras, no misses, no miscount to report.

The mutation was proven to land on disk before the reading was taken (marker counts flipped 1→0 and 0→1; blob hash `5635797…` → `fe15dce…`), and the restore leg was verified by hash equality against the `HEAD` blob rather than by an exit code, under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths. `@object-ui/react` is vitest-aliased to `packages/react/src`, so no build stands between the edit and the run and there is no stale-`dist` failure mode here.

Green on both legs, as predicted: `SchemaRenderer.primitiveSchema.test.tsx`, `SchemaRenderer.propsResolution.test.ts`, `data-table-empty-action-primitive-node.test.tsx`, `empty-action-declared-7105.test.tsx`, `overlay-node-slot-doc-types-7082.test.ts`.

## Verification

| what | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| targeted suites (2 new + 5 existing pins) | `pnpm exec vitest run` on those 7 paths | `Test Files 7 passed (7)`, `Tests 77 passed (77)` |
| affected packages, full | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/ packages/components/` | `Test Files 336 passed (336)`, `Tests 3273 passed (3273)` |
| type-check | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react --filter @object-ui/components run type-check` | both `Done` (this is what checks the compile-time pins) |
| lint | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/react --filter @object-ui/components run lint` | exit 0, `0 errors` (948 pre-existing warnings, none on the changed lines) |
| build | `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/react..." --filter "@object-ui/components..." run build` | exit 0 |
| gates | `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major` | all exit 0 |

`NOT MEASURED: check:sdui-registration-pins, reason: PREREQUISITE NOT MET — it reads the built console bundle and asks for `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` first; declared to CI. Its subject did not move: the diff to `empty.tsx` is comment lines only (verified), and no registration bytes changed anywhere.` Everything else repo-wide is CI's run, not mine.

## Snapshots in the brief that did not survive re-derivation

- **`app-shell` has zero call sites.** Control: 50 files there mention `SchemaRenderer`, so the scan reaches the package and finds things in it. The card's list also omits `apps/site` (5 — the very package the docblock records breaking `Build Docs`), `examples/schema-catalog` (12) and `packages/plugin-map` (1). "Roughly fourteen" is exactly right for the four packages the card listed that really do have sites; the *set* was wrong, not the arithmetic.
- **The card's six-row table is six VALUES, not six members** — it samples `string` / `number` / `boolean` twice each and never touches `BaseSchema`, `null` or `undefined`. A "pin all six members" suite built from that table would have missed half the union, which is why the members were enumerated from the declaration instead.
- Confirmed unchanged on today's tree: the renderer still narrows `!evaluatedSchema` **above** the `String(…)` defensive branch, and the evaluation memo returns every primitive untouched, so the card's mechanism holds exactly as written.

## Acceptance notes

- **Filed as objectui#9033** while enumerating call sites: `header-bar`'s `rightContent` slot still guards with an `&&` chain, so `rightContent: 0` leaks the raw number and paints a stray "0" — the numeric-falsy JSX trap objectui#8331 closed one slot over. **This change does NOT close it**: the `&&` short-circuits before the bridge is ever called. Measured through the real renderer stack (`"Toggle Sidebar0"` against a `"Toggle Sidebar"` baseline), probe deleted, tree verified clean. It is the only remaining instance in the tree. Deliberately not fixed here — different mechanism, different file, and the guard's truthiness-vs-nullish question deserves its own ruling now that the bridge is honest.
- The pending `.changeset/8331-…md` release note contains one sentence this change falsifies (the bridge's `String` mapping "would otherwise turn them into the text `"0"` and `"false"`"). I did not edit another card's release note; my changeset explicitly supersedes that sentence instead, so a reader of the combined CHANGELOG is not left with the contradiction. Noted, not filed — the successor text ships in the same release.
